claims: On a frozen 200-prompt set, the shipped quantized package running on the phone raises the mean per-token negative log-likelihood of the original model's own greedy continuations by 0.0213 nats/token over the original FP32 model; the pre-registered limit was 0.05.
No subset exceeds 0.029 (limit 0.15) and no item exceeds 0.102 (limit 0.40); the phone's argmax agrees with the reference continuation on 95.1% of tokens.

en.kind: English, single turn (explanation, writing, reasoning, everyday advice)

zh.kind: Simplified Chinese, single turn, topics parallel to the English subset but not translations

multi.kind: multi-turn: 4 user turns and 3 fixed assistant turns (20 English, 20 Chinese)

code.kind: write, explain or fix code (Python, Swift, SQL, JavaScript, C, Rust, Go, TypeScript, shell)

long.kind: long input (>= 1,500 tokens) built from unpublished first-party documents and source code plus a task, mixed English and Chinese

testSet.contents: not published: the long subset contains unpublished text; only the hashes and aggregate results are released
testSet.rendering: the checkpoint's own chat template, thinking disabled, no system prompt, generation prompt appended; the phone consumes the frozen token ids
testSet.references: continuations generated by the original model (greedy, at most 128 tokens, ending at a stop token if one is produced), frozen before any candidate was judged
testSet.baseline: the original checkpoint evaluated in FP32 (bf16 weights widened to FP32 before each matmul) on a Mac CPU, one unpadded teacher-forced pass per item

metric.definition: mean negative log-likelihood (nats/token) of the reference continuation tokens under teacher forcing; prompt and template tokens excluded; delta = candidate - baseline, token-weighted
metric.secondary: greedy agreement (argmax equals the reference token), recorded only
metric.candidateComputation: product engine on the phone, FP16 logits from the head, accumulated in double precision, no per-token logits written to disk

reproducibilityNote: the 200 per-item NLL sums equalled, bit for bit, those of an earlier Debug run of the 4096-capacity package on an iPhone 17 Pro with iOS 27.0

formatAlternatives.note: Mac PyTorch recomputations of the exported graph with each format's rounding, on subsets of the same set, measured while choosing the format; only lut6 was then run on the phone on all 200 items

rows.format: all projections INT8 per channel (FP32 model with the package rounding)
MLP INT4 per channel, head INT4
rows.note: after restricting INT4 to gate/up/down; an exporter error that also quantized the per-layer-embedding projections to INT4 had given +0.750

rows.format: MLP lut4 (16-entry palette per 16 channels), head INT4
MLP lut4 on gate and up only

formatAlternatives.layerSensitivity: switching one layer's gate/up from FP32 to lut4 at a time (6 items) cost at most +0.004 per layer, spread over layers 11-41: no small set of layers carried the loss

details.note: per-layer-embedding projections live in the MLP module; quantizing them with the MLP to INT4 was an exporter error, fixed by keeping them INT8
